content.summary: The source map supports the required inherited design and high-point statements without importing I(27) into those structural lemmas. The public preprint independently retrieved in this round matches the manuscript conventions and explicitly supplies the external intersecting bound; the public A1K report matches the inherited conditional endpoint. The f(4,3) notation issue is resolved. The minimum-transversal classification is implemented by a local wrapper around inherited component facts, which is a valid dependency and does not threaten the theorem.

findings.statement: Section 1 now defines f(4,3) as the maximum cardinality and gives the forcing-threshold conversion f(4,3)+1.
findings.disposition: The off-by-one convention ambiguity identified in round 1 is closed.

findings.statement: The ordinary corollary uses the external canonical enumeration, while the inherited structural inputs are represented by local Lean theorems; a source-closure bundle is not an independent replay of the external enumeration.
findings.disposition: Maintain the existing external-I(27) and same-evaluator qualifications.

revisions.action: Checked the newly explicit maximum-size definition and forcing-threshold sentence in Section 1.
revisions.result: The intended convention is now unambiguous and agrees with the primary preprint.

checks.scope: Inherited degree-twenty design and transversal dependency map
checks.method: Inspected frozen portable sources Erdos20ExtremalTwenty.lean lines 219-254, Erdos20ExtremalTransversals.lean lines 37-96, Erdos20V8Stability.lean lines 51-78, and MinimumTransversals.lean lines 9-81.
checks.observation: The two-design theorem requires only triple uniformity, sunflower-freeness and cardinality twenty, and supplies disjoint six-point supports, point degree five, and pair codegree two. The inherited transversal lower bound is six; the local classification of all minimum six-transversals follows by splitting into the two supports and applying the inherited three-transversal iff block lemma. No I(27) assumption occurs in these interfaces.

checks.scope: Global high-point bound and exact boundary dependencies
checks.method: Read the frozen high_points_card_le_two signature in Erdos20V12HighCardTwo.lean lines 88-94 and the literal profiles plus terminal reduction in Erdos20V13Boundary.lean lines 25-73.
checks.observation: The at-most-two-high-point theorem is unconditional on I(27), cardinality and support. The profile reduction is explicitly conditional on I(27), and its realizability definitions include actual uniform sunflower-free families of cardinality 81 and the no-two-highs-per-member condition. Thus the theorem inputs are not merely numerical censuses.

checks.scope: Primary-source agreement and remaining external gap
checks.method: Actually opened https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06175v1 and https://a1k.ai/agentic-math/rank-four-sunflower-free-families with web.run and inspected the relevant source sections; compared with the frozen ledger.
checks.observation: The arXiv source defines f by maximum size, permits empty cores, and gives the intersecting maximum in Proposition 6.8 using the upper enumeration of Proposition 6.7. Its numerical global bound is 83. The A1K public report states the unconditional high-point theorem and conditional bound 81, leaving the final eighty obligations open. I did not rerun the external enumeration or establish exhaustive priority.
